pools.pool: category npc: the people are the opening
keyGuarantees: the settlement carries hooks of category npc
pools.ruling: Scoped: it renders under a crisis and line 4 says very little here is a crisis.

lines.text: What is worth doing in {settlement} is worth doing because of who is in it; the town's difficulties have names attached before they have causes.
{settlement}'s open questions sit with particular people rather than with offices, which is what makes them approachable.
A stranger with business in {settlement} will be pointed at a person, not at an institution.
{settlement}'s people are individually consequential and collectively agreed; there is a great deal here to get involved with and very little of it is a crisis.

pools.pool: category faction: the blocs are the opening
keyGuarantees: the settlement carries hooks of category faction
pools.ruling: Colour, not scoped: bloc politics asserts no calm.

lines.text: {settlement}'s live questions are questions between groups, and each group would rather have a third party settle it than concede.
Nothing in {settlement} gets decided by one person, which means everything in {settlement} can be influenced.
{settlement} has more than one authority and no arbiter, and that gap is where anyone from outside would be useful.
The blocs in {settlement} are close enough in strength that a small weight put on either side would be felt.

pools.pool: category tension: the standing quarrels are the opening
keyGuarantees: the settlement carries hooks of category tension
pools.ruling: Scoped: line 2 sets its difficulties apart from a crisis and line 4 says nothing is about to break; both are false under an active crisis.

lines.text: {settlement} runs on arrangements that everyone here has agreed not to test, and the untested places are where the town is soft.
{settlement}'s difficulties are recorded, chronic and unresolved, which is a different opportunity from a crisis.
What is wrong in {settlement} is not hidden. It is simply nobody's job.
{settlement} carries its quarrels well and carries them all the time; nothing here is about to break, and nothing here is about to be fixed either.

pools.pool: category economics: the books are the opening
keyGuarantees: the settlement carries hooks of category economics
pools.ruling: Colour, not scoped: a supply gap is a pressure, not a calm.

lines.text: What {settlement} needs and what {settlement} can get do not line up, and the gap is a standing invitation to anyone who can close it.
The trouble in {settlement} is a supply question before it is anything else, and supply questions are answerable by outsiders.
{settlement} is short of something specific, and being short of something specific is the most tractable kind of difficulty a town can have.
{settlement}'s margin is thin enough that a change in what arrives would change what the town does.

pools.pool: category safety: the streets are the opening
keyGuarantees: the settlement carries hooks of category safety
pools.ruling: Scoped: lines 4-5 call the town safer than its country, false under a threat (siege, occupation, monsters) or unrest crisis.

lines.text: {settlement} has more trouble than it has people to answer it, and the shortfall is where the work is.
What {settlement} reports and what {settlement} suffers differ by enough that the difference is itself the opening.
{settlement} is a town where being competent and armed makes you immediately useful, and the town knows it.
{settlement} is safer than its country, and what threatens it comes from outside the walls rather than inside them.
{settlement} is safer than its country, and what threatens it comes from the country around it rather than from within.

pools.pool: category history: the past is the opening
keyGuarantees: the settlement carries hooks of category history
pools.ruling: Colour, not scoped: speaks of the past.

lines.text: {settlement} has business with its own past that has not finished, and the unfinished parts are on the record rather than in dispute.
Things that happened at {settlement} still have consequences with nobody assigned to them.
{settlement} would rather not revisit certain things, which is a reliable sign that revisiting them would produce something.
The reason {settlement} is the way it is lies further back than anyone here will volunteer.

pools.pool: category relationship: the ties are the opening
keyGuarantees: the settlement carries hooks of category relationship
pools.ruling: Colour, not scoped: ties and obligations assert no calm.

lines.text: What binds people in {settlement} also obliges them, and the obligations do not all point the same way.
{settlement}'s ties are dense enough that a favour asked of one person reaches three, and everyone here knows which three.
Getting anything done in {settlement} means going through somebody, and going through somebody has a price that is rarely money.
Two of {settlement}'s ties are pulling against each other, and the people caught between them have not yet chosen.

keyGuarantees: a live bread_riot clock: the food supply chain is strained or worse
pools.ruling: Scoped: line 4 says the strain is only an expensive season thanks to the granary, false under a hunger crisis.

lines.text: {settlement}'s food comes through a chain that is under strain, and a chain under strain has a shape to how it fails.
The price of bread in {settlement} is the number this town watches, and it is going the wrong way.
{settlement} can absorb what is happening to its food for a while, and the while is what everyone here is quietly estimating.
{settlement}'s food chain is strained and its granary is not; what would be a crisis in a town without stores is, here, an expensive season.

keyGuarantees: a live smuggling_rise clock: lawful trade is strained
pools.ruling: Not scoped: no line asserts a calm a crisis contradicts; the watch and gate are presence presumptions.

lines.text: {settlement}'s lawful trade is under strain, and where lawful trade thins, something else has room.
What is not coming into {settlement} through the gate is a gap, and gaps in a town like this get filled.
{settlement}'s revenue depends on trade passing where it can be counted, and less of it is passing there.
{settlement}'s trade is strained and its watch is not distracted; the gap is real and nobody has yet been able to work it.

keyGuarantees: a live legitimacy_crisis clock: the governing power's legitimacy is contested
pools.ruling: Scoped: lines 3-4 say no rival claim or opposition exists, false under a succession or unrest crisis.

lines.text: {governing} governs {settlement} and does not command it, and the difference is audible in the market.
Instructions from {settlement}'s hall are being complied with slowly, which is how a town says no without saying it.
{governing}'s standing in {settlement} rests on nobody yet having a better claim.
{governing} is contested in {settlement} and unopposed; the town's complaint is real and has nowhere to go.

keyGuarantees: a live faction_split clock: two factions hold overlapping ground
pools.ruling: Scoped: line 4 says the division holds, false under a succession or unrest crisis.

lines.text: {faction} and {faction2} hold overlapping ground in {settlement} and want incompatible things with it.
Two powers in {settlement} need the same rooms, and the rooms are not getting larger.
The people of {settlement} who deal with both {faction} and {faction2} are the ones who will have to choose first.
{faction} and {faction2} overlap in {settlement} and have divided the overlap; the arrangement holds, and it holds on one person's word.
